title: Polynomial-time transduction of finite-state words
statement: Let $S$ be a finite state set with decidable equality, let $\mathrm{next}:S\times\{0,1\}\to S$ be a state update, let $\mathrm{emit}:S\times\{0,1\}\to\mathrm{Option}(\{0,1\})$ specify an optional output bit for each state and input bit, and let $\mathrm{finish}:S\to\mathrm{Option}(\{0,1\})$ specify an optional final output bit. For every start state, the word function that processes the input bits in order using these rules and appends the final output is polynomial-time computable.
replaced: Every finite one-way word transducer computes its recursive word semantics within time equal to the input length plus one, and is in particular polynomial-time computable.
